Why I'm worried: BrightWave is hitting production traffic patterns that might trigger our concurrency cap/backpressure loops and cause head-of-line blocking for other tenants. They are an enterprise customer on a committed plan (BW-ENT-2025-09) and this is affecting revenue and their promotions.

- David: quick triage on token/concurrency rejection counts and delay queue depth.

Quick triage notes from the 09:45 call and initial log passes:
- We see a strong correlation between p99 spikes and short burst windows where request "bursts" push per-worker queue depth to >80%. The request token limiter is configured at 64 concurrent requests per worker for this model variant; during bursts many requests overflow into the backlog which then triggers backpressure and occasional 429/500 proxy errors downstream.
- Autoscaler reacted to CPU/RT spikes by scaling down a few workers during the worst windows; that reduced total capacity briefly and amplified queue depth — classic backpressure oscillation.
- Trace excerpts show head-of-line blocking in the prefix KV cache warmup path — a few cold prefixes caused long kernel execution which delayed subsequent requests.

Proposed immediate mitigations (safe, quick):
1) Temporarily increase per-worker concurrency cap from 64 -> 96 for BrightWave's route (can be toggled at the routing layer). Low risk for model correctness; watch memory.
2) Enable short LRU prefix caching for this customer to reduce cold-prefix stalls (config flag).
3) Adjust autoscaler cooldown: extend the scale-down cooldown by 2m to prevent premature shrink during transient spikes.

I'll attach the initial-triage-notes (logs trimmed). If approved I'll execute 1 & 2 as a hotfix and monitor p99 for 30m windows.

— David
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FW: Spike in tail latency and 500s — BrightWave checkout

Adding deeper analysis from model/infra side:
- Reproduced the backpressure signature in staging when introducing bursty traffic with a small number of cold prefix seeds. The behavior is an oscillation: bursts -> queue backlog -> autoscaler scales down (due to noisy cpu sampling) -> backlog persists -> more workers get overloaded -> 500s/429s increase.
- The model-runner showed a small number of long kernel invocations tied to attention reshape paths (rare, but high cost). Combined with per-worker concurrency caps this creates cascading delays.

Recommended actions (short + medium):
Short-term (apply now):
- Apply David's concurrency cap bump for BW route and enable prefix caching.
- Increase autoscaler scale-down cooldown and add a small buffer to the node-set minimum for BW traffic.

Medium-term (postmortem):
- Add an adaptive concurrency limiter that smooths bursts instead of immediate rejection (token-bucket with a short refill window).
- Investigate kernel scheduling priority for cold-prefix traces and tune attention reshape kernels to avoid 10-20x outliers.

Risks: the concurrency bump increases memory pressure per worker; monitor OOM and swap. Prefix caching will have clear cache-population transient effects but should reduce cold-path hits.

I'll run the hotfixs after sign-off from Monica (for customer-facing comms) and ops.

— Nikhil Sharma
ML Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

Alex / BrightWave ops — update and actions we've completed: 

What happened:
- Short bursty traffic windows plus a few cold-prefix kernel outliers caused worker queue depth to spike and our autoscaler to mis-time scale-downs, producing a backpressure oscillation and higher p99/p99.9. That in turn caused downstream 500s and reduced observed throughput.

Actions taken (hotfix, 07/02–07/04):
1) Temporarily increased per-worker concurrency cap for your checkout route from 64 -> 96 (rolled back if memory alarms trigger).
2) Enabled short LRU prefix caching for the route to mitigate cold-prefix stalls.
3) Extended autoscaler scale-down cooldown and raised node minimum buffer for the BrightWave traffic pool.
4) Opened JIRA SUP-1234 and linked the HubSpot contact (BW-12345).
5) Monitoring: we are watching p99/p99.9 and error rate in 5m and 30m windows. Early numbers show p99 down ~60% in the latest window and 500s falling back to baseline.

Next steps / commitments:
- We will run an internal postmortem by 2026-07-07 with root cause write-up and medium-term mitigation plan (adaptive limiter + kernel tuning).
- We will offer BrightWave a service credit for the impacted windows — Marissa will follow up with ACV/credit options.
- If you want, we can provision a short-term dedicated pool for your checkout route to provide isolation during the holiday window.
